text:
Alex (AE): Quick help — we're at signature stage for the POC with Meridian Health. Procurement is insisting on a 3-way e-sign (customer + reseller + Redwood) because reseller will issue the PO. They also pushed back on SLA language in Section 4 and want DPA scoping clarified. Can legal + ops advise on routing and fallback?
Sam (SalesOps): Heard. Do we have the reseller name and contact? Also need to know if reseller is set up for DocuSign or prefers Adobe Sign.
Alex (AE): Reseller = InterBridge Solutions, contact is carla@interbridge.co. They said they "cannot do embedded signing" — only standard DocuSign or manual signed PDF.
Maria (Legal): Ok. Two quick asks: 1) send redline PDF they returned, 2) confirm whether customer will countersign before or after reseller. If reseller signs first we may need a three-party signature order clause. 
Alex (AE): Uploaded their redline here: https://files.redwood.example/meridian_redline_v1.pdf — main changes are SLA uptime target and indemnity carveouts. They also inserted a clause requiring access logs be retained 7 years.
Chen (Security): FYI they attached a short security questionnaire (SSQ). Link: https://files.redwood.example/meridian_ssq_v2.xlsx — questions on data residency and KMS. I flagged KMS as "requires enterprise/private deployment" for some endpoints.
Priya (Solutions): On the POC itself: we agreed hosted API with isolated project keys. We can confirm region (us-east) and not expose KMS to reseller. That should address most SSQ pts.
Maria (Legal): For signature routing — we prefer the simplest reliable path. Options:
- Option A: 2-step then 3rd acknowledgement: Customer signs MSA + Orderform; reseller signs separately and we record reseller acceptance via countersign or PO upload.
- Option B: True 3-way DocuSign envelope with routing order (Reseller -> Customer -> Redwood).
Option B is cleaner but depends on reseller DocuSign capability.
Sam (SalesOps): InterBridge said no embedded, but they have DocuSign. So Option B possible. However if they refuse DocuSign API routing we may need fallback.
Alex (AE): What fallback looks like?
Sam (SalesOps): Fallback: Reseller signs their paper copy, scans and emails PDF to procurement@meridian.com cc: legal@redwood.com. SalesOps then uploads to contract record and marks as "reseller-signed". Then customer signs via DocuSign and we countersign. It's clunkier but workable.
Maria (Legal): Maria here — prefer Option B but accept fallback if we get: (a) scanned PDF with signature block + date, (b) PO number and email trail confirming intent, (c) exec sign-off from reseller (title). Also need to resolve SLA redline: propose we keep SLA as-is but add Service Credits table with capped remedies and an audit window of 90 days instead of 7 years for logs.
Alex (AE): Meridian procurement insists 7 years for logs. Can we offer 3 years with legal access on subpoena?
Maria (Legal): Counter: 3 years standard, we can add a carveout for regulatory requests with an agreement to cooperate. For indemnity they removed limitation — we should keep our standard lim on consequential damages.
Chen (Security): 7 years retention is high risk. Recommend 3 years and justify. Also for KMS: we can offer customer-managed keys on Redwood Private for enterprise customers but not for hosted POC. Need to call that out in the SSQ response.
Priya (Solutions): For the POC timeline, we need signed orderform by EOD Friday to hit deploy window. If signature routing stalls, we lose the slot.
Alex (AE): Noted — timeline pressure. @Maria, can you confirm whether legal can accept 3-way DocuSign with routing order and standard countersign from Redwood? If yes we'll ask reseller to set up envelope and include these recipient roles: Reseller (signer), Customer (signer), Redwood (signer).
Maria (Legal): Yes, we can accept that. Need the envelope roles + email addresses and final PDF. Also please include Appendix A with the limited SLA remedy language I uploaded: https://files.redwood.example/appendixA_sla_draft.pdf
Sam (SalesOps): I'll send InterBridge a DocuSign template request. If they decline, I'll implement fallback workflow and capture PO scan + email chain. I'll also run the /docusign create-envelope command once we have final PDFs:
```
/docusign create-envelope --template poc-order --recipients "reseller:carla@interbridge.co,customer:pm@meridian.com,redwood:contracts@redwood.com" --routing-order "1,2,3"
```
Alex (AE): Perfect. One more — pricing question from procurement: they asked if we can move to Net45 instead of Net30 for the POC invoice. Is that okay?
Sam (SalesOps): Finance ok with Net45 for POC under $10k. I'll note in orderform Payment Terms: Net45 (PO required).
Maria (Legal): Confirming next steps from Legal side: I'll review their redlines and send a tracked counterproposal by tomorrow morning. If they accept SLA appendix and log retention to 3 years we'll sign. Otherwise escalate to execs.
Alex (AE): Thanks all — I'll ping Carla and Meridian PM with routing plan and deadline. :thumbsup:
Dana-bot: Reminder — deployment window at risk if orderform not countersigned by 1717119600.
Sam (SalesOps): Action items: Sam -> send DocuSign template request to InterBridge; Maria -> counterproposal; Chen -> SSQ answers (highlight KMS limitation); Priya -> finalize orderform with Net45. I'll update CRM with "3-way e-sign planned".
Alex (AE): Going to copy this thread into the deal record and tag execs if needed. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Maria (Legal): Will post the redline counter in this thread when ready.
Alex (AE): Closing notes: keep communications in-thread to preserve audit trail. Thanks!
